title: How Britain Defeated ‘Assisted Dying’
author: Dan Hitchens
content:
![How Britain Defeated ‘Assisted
Dying’](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/09/GettyImages-2294124729.jpg)

Every developed country faces a deeply uncomfortable problem: People are
getting older. This means a fiscal crisis sometime in the coming decades,
because it results in more dependents on the welfare state and fewer
taxpayers. Equally, it means a cultural crisis, because the habits of mutual
dependence and reverence for age are being eaten away by the culture of Now.
Simply put, we don't know what to do with the dependent and unproductive
people in our midst.

No wonder some people are mulling the obvious solution. Writing for the
leading magazine of the British left, _The New Statesman_ , the commentator
Oli Dugmore recently[ _observed_](https://www.newstatesman.com/politics/uk-
politics/2025/09/let-them-die?ref=compactmag.com): "All over the country our
elders sit in cell blocks bathed in the stupefying light and sound of _Bargain
Hunt_ , _Location, Location, Location_ , _Tipping Point_ , unvisited by
relatives who are preoccupied by the rhythm of their lives, or perhaps unable
to summon the courage to witness the degeneration of the once totemic figures
of their lives, their mum and dad." His answer: "Let them die."

That exhortation was a reference to the assisted suicide bill, which
Parliament voted on for the last time on Friday. The legislation, Dugmore
said, would not only rid us of those awkward inhabitants of care homes but
would drive down "the pensions bill, the NHS bill and the care bill." Everyone
wins except, perhaps, the people receiving a dose of lethal drugs. But then it
was their choice. Or maybe it wasn't exactly, but never mind.
